references.text: Jacob's love for Rachel and his agreement with Laban to serve seven years for her.
Laban gives Leah to Jacob at night instead of Rachel—the deception discovered in the morning.
Laban's explanation and new agreement: Jacob must serve another seven years to get Rachel.
Esau complains that Jacob deceived him—a strong thematic parallel where the deceiver is now himself deceived.
Jacob complains that Laban has changed his wages ten times—a pattern of deception from Laban.
Jacob's summary of his twenty years with Laban, marked by hard work and unfair treatment.
'What a man sows, he will also reap'—a principle illustrated as Jacob himself experiences deception after deceiving his brother.
Mirroring accusations: Laban uses the same rhetoric against Jacob that Jacob used against him earlier, underscoring the theme of mutual deception and conflict.
A clear thematic parallel about broken expectations: An ally (Laban/Balaam) does the opposite of what was agreed upon, creating a deep theological contrast between human planning and outcomes.
